exam_scheme.note: The International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) Selection Programme in India is conducted jointly by the Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education (HBCSE - TIFR), the National Board for Higher Mathematics (NBHM), and the Mathematics Teachers’ Association (India) [MTA(I)]. The selection process is a multi-tier competition pathway for secondary and higher secondary school students to select the official 6-member Indian team for the International Mathematical Olympiad: Stage 1 is the Indian Olympiad Qualifier in Mathematics (IOQM), an objective OMR test of 30 integer-answer questions (100 marks, 180 minutes). Stage 2 is the Regional Mathematical Olympiad (RMO), a 3-hour descriptive examination consisting of 6 proof-based mathematical problems. Stage 3 is the Indian National Mathematical Olympiad (INMO), a 4.5-hour (270 minutes) examination consisting of 6 advanced proof problems administered to ~600 qualifiers across India. The top ~35 students from INMO attend the International Mathematical Olympiad Training Camp (IMOTC) at HBCSE (Stage 4), where selection tests determine the final 6 students who represent India at the International Mathematical Olympiad (Stage 5).

Top ~35 students receive INMO Merit Award and qualify for Stage 4 IMOTC at HBCSE
